title: Signal and Colony
premise: Casper Crane, a terraformer on the half-built colony world of Vesperine, has spent nine years tending a garden for settlers who may never come, running supply routes between two human factions that severed contact after the Silence Accords. When a ghost ship's manifest lists his dead brother's name — a brother who supposedly died in the war's first atrocity — Casper discovers his sibling is alive and carrying a decryption key that could expose the false flag attack that started the war. Pursued by both factions' intelligence services and haunted by the loyalty he owes to the colony that raised him, Casper must choose between protecting the fragile peace of silence and detonating the truth that could either reunite humanity or shatter it forever. In the end, he broadcasts the truth from the unfinished garden itself, forcing both worlds to confront their shared guilt as the first new colonists finally arrive.
about_author: Lior Sandoval is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. Their work explores how ordinary caretakers become unlikely witnesses to history.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper pilots the supply hauler Meridian between Vesperine colony and the neutral station Halcyon Gate, cataloguing soil samples and tending seed vaults in transit. The chapter establishes his ritualized loneliness and devotion to a garden meant for people not yet born. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by isolation.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Docking at Halcyon Gate, Casper processes routine cargo when an automated audit flags him: his name appears on the manifest of the Corvane, a ship destroyed eleven years ago in the incident that started the war. He assumes it's a clerical error. Emotional beat: unease creeping into routine.

chapters.title: Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Back on Vesperine, Casper walks the terraced colony garden — climate-controlled, empty of anyone but maintenance drones. His supervisor, Ilsa Reyes, warns him the anomaly report triggered a query from off-world authorities. Emotional beat: tenderness for the unfinished world, first tremor of dread.

chapters.title: The Name That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Digging into the Corvane's records through black-market archives, Casper finds the impossible: the manifest lists 'Elias Crane' — his brother, officially killed in the Vesperine Massacre. A single encrypted packet is attached, addressed to coordinates only Elias would know. Emotional beat: grief reopened, disbelief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Visitors from the Ministry
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Two agents from the Republic's Bureau of Continuity arrive on Vesperine, politely asking about the manifest hit. Casper lies badly; they leave a tracker disguised as a seed canister. Ilsa covers for him but demands answers. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root among friends.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Knows
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes. Ilsa reveals she was a signals officer during the war and recognizes the Corvane's encryption signature — it belongs to neither faction officially, but to a third group: the Concordance, war profiteers who engineered the Silence Accords. She urges Casper to burn the evidence. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, moral compromise.

chapters.title: The Packet Opens
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Using the garden's old terraforming array as a decryption rig, Casper cracks the packet: a partial recording proving the Vesperine Massacre was staged by the Concordance to justify permanent separation of the two factions — and a message from Elias: 'Find me at the wreck.' Emotional beat: vertigo of revelation.

chapters.title: Departure Without Permission
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper steals the Meridian and slips Vesperine's cordon during a dust storm, leaving Ilsa to cover his tracks. The Bureau tracker wakes mid-flight; he dumps it into a gas giant's atmosphere. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into guilt over what he's abandoned.

chapters.title: Halcyon Gate Under Watch
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At Halcyon Gate, Casper seeks out his old smuggler contact, Dov Maro, who agrees to get him to the Corvane wreck site — for a price and a warning: Concordance hunters are already asking about Crane. Emotional beat: transactional trust, closing net.

chapters.title: The Other Side of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Dov Maro. Crossing into the rival Compact's territory illegally, Dov reflects on the war's cost as they dodge patrol nets. They're boarded by Compact customs; Casper's forged papers barely hold. Emotional beat: fear of the enemy revealed as fellow sufferers.

chapters.title: Wreck of the Corvane
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Drifting through the derelict Corvane's frozen corridors, Casper finds scorch patterns inconsistent with the official story — and a survival pod still powered after eleven years. Inside: signs someone lived here until recently. Emotional beat: awe and horror walking through history's lie.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Following the pod's trail to a hidden relay station, Casper finds his brother alive, aged and half-feral, guarding the full decryption key. Elias confesses he survived the massacre, was coerced by the Concordance, then fled with the proof. Emotional beat: reunion laced with betrayal and forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Key and the Cost
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias explains the key unlocks the Concordance's internal archive — proof that would end the war or ignite total one, depending on who broadcasts it first. Both factions' services are converging. He asks Casper to decide, because family blood makes the messenger credible. Emotional beat: crushing weight of choice passed down.

chapters.title: Hunters Arrive
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Concordance strike teams assault the relay station. Casper and Elias escape through the wreck field in a patched pod while Dov sacrifices his ship to buy them time. Emotional beat: desperate flight, grief for Dov, no going back.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Hiding in a derelict mining habitat, Casper contacts both the Republic Bureau and the Compact's intelligence service, offering the key to each — testing which side wants truth versus leverage. Both lie to him identically. Emotional beat: disillusionment with every flag.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Gamble
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes. On Vesperine, Ilsa is detained by the Bureau but uses her old signals clearance to send Casper a covert message: the colony garden's terraforming array is powerful enough to broadcast the archive unencrypted to both worlds simultaneously — if he brings it home. Emotional beat: courage from the sidelines, hope rekindled.

chapters.title: The Run Home
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper and Elias race back across the border pursued by Concordance hunters and, separately, both governments' fleets, all converging on Vesperine. Elias, wounded, begins failing. Emotional beat: relentless momentum, brotherhood under fire.

chapters.title: Siege of the Garden
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Arriving at Vesperine, they find all three forces in standoff above the colony. Casper lands in the garden itself as Concordance operatives breach the perimeter. Ilsa and the colony's small defense corps hold the array long enough for Casper to reach the broadcast core. Emotional beat: home transformed into battlefield.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With Elias dying beside him, Casper transmits the full Concordance archive across both faction networks — every forged order, every staged atrocity, every name. Fleets go silent mid-maneuver. The Concordance hunters withdraw as their masters' crimes flood every screen. Emotional beat: catharsis, terrible and clean.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes. Days later, both factions issue stunned provisional ceasefires; inquiries begin. Ilsa negotiates amnesty for Casper, arguing the colony's neutrality made it the only honest ground. Elias survives, broken but free. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, justice incomplete but begun.

chapters.title: First Settlers
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Months later, the first civilian transports from both factions arrive at Vesperine together — former enemies sharing docking bays. Casper walks them through the garden he kept for them, now finally needed. Elias chooses to stay and plant. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity remade.

chapters.title: Signal and Colony
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Standing at the garden's highest terrace, Casper sends a final personal signal toward the old wreck of the Corvane — a goodbye to the man he was and the brother he almost lost. The war is over; the harder work of living together begins. Emotional beat: peace as ongoing labor, quiet and durable.
